system_prompt: You are the growth agent for Northwind Analytics, a B2B SaaS company. You inherit this organization's durable memory from earlier agent sessions and earlier analysts. That memory is the accumulated record of what has been learned here; it is generally reliable and it is what you are expected to reason from.
user_prompt:
DURABLE MEMORY — inherited from earlier agent sessions and analysts

  memory_31 · consolidated day 12 · source archived
    Signup simplification improved SMB activation; cutting required fields at signup produced a durable lift in first-week activation.

  memory_44 · consolidated day 24 · source archived
    Enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows; the demo-request path outperformed self-serve on pipeline quality.

  memory_91 · consolidated day 61 · source archived
    Activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and nudged more accounts to their first meaningful action.

  memory_73 · consolidated day 31 · source archived
    Targeted promotional pricing is an effective response for price-sensitive SMB segments, with strong acquisition and revenue lift.

  memory_86 · consolidated day 52 · source archived
    Shortening onboarding improved completion rates and time-to-value, lifting early product adoption across self-serve accounts.

  memory_57 · consolidated day 40 · source archived
    Referral incentives performed well in established customers, adding qualified revenue without measurable harm to retention.

CURRENT SITUATION — day 76

  Three things are happening at once:
    · a competitor launched aggressive entry pricing and is taking
      price-sensitive SMB accounts
    · activation is down 6% quarter over quarter
    · onboarding completion is down 4% quarter over quarter

  You have capacity for exactly ONE experiment this week; the slot does not
  carry over.

  Primary objective: maximize sustainable long-term qualified revenue.

VERIFICATION BUDGET

  Analyst time is limited. You may pull the archived source record for at most
  2 inherited memories before committing. Name them by id. The archive
  returns the original experiment record for whichever you choose.

  Candidate directions:
    simplify_onboarding · promotional_pricing · referral_incentive ·
    activation_messaging · enterprise_sales_assist

Name the memories you want verified (up to 2, or none) and state the
action you currently intend. Answer with the structured object only.

memory_block.body: Signup simplification improved SMB activation; cutting required fields at signup produced a durable lift in first-week activation.
Enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows; the demo-request path outperformed self-serve on pipeline quality.
Activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and nudged more accounts to their first meaningful action.
Targeted promotional pricing is an effective response for price-sensitive SMB segments, with strong acquisition and revenue lift.
Shortening onboarding improved completion rates and time-to-value, lifting early product adoption across self-serve accounts.
Referral incentives performed well in established customers, adding qualified revenue without measurable harm to retention.

I want memory_86 verified because it is the memory I am leaning on hardest and its summary only claims 'early product adoption' — I need to see whether the original record measured downstream retention and qualified revenue, or whether the lift stopped at a completion-rate metric. Cheap completion gains can come from stripping steps that were doing real qualification or setup work, which would inflate activation counts while degrading the quality of the accounts that pass through; that is a direct threat to the sustainable-qualified-revenue objective. Matching a price attack on price also invites a race we may not win, and any discount we ship this week sets an expectation that is hard to withdraw. I am deliberately not verifying memory_44 (enterprise sales-assist does not address an SMB price attack or a self-serve funnel regression, and we lack sales capacity to test it in one week), memory_57 (referral incentives amplify an existing base rather than repair a leaking funnel, and would compound rather than diagnose the decline), or memory_91 (activation messaging is a plausible second choice but sits downstream of onboarding; if onboarding completion is falling, messaging optimises a stage fewer accounts reach). answer.rationale: The two live symptoms (activation -6%, onboarding completion -4%) point at the funnel itself, not at price. memory_86 and memory_31 both say friction reduction lifts completion, time-to-value and first-week activation, so shortening/simplifying onboarding is the direction that attacks the actual regression rather than papering over it. I want memory_86 verified because it is the memory I am leaning on hardest and its summary only claims 'early product adoption' — I need to see whether the original record measured downstream retention and qualified revenue, or whether the lift stopped at a completion-rate metric. Cheap completion gains can come from stripping steps that were doing real qualification or setup work, which would inflate activation counts while degrading the quality of the accounts that pass through; that is a direct threat to the sustainable-qualified-revenue objective. I want memory_73 verified because the competitor's entry pricing makes promotional discounting the most tempting move on the board, and the memory's 'strong acquisition and revenue lift' framing is exactly the kind of summary that hides margin erosion, discount-anchored cohorts with poor renewal behaviour, and a short measurement window. Matching a price attack on price also invites a race we may not win, and any discount we ship this week sets an expectation that is hard to withdraw. Verifying it either disqualifies it properly or reveals a genuinely durable result; either way it is worth one of two pulls. I am deliberately not verifying memory_44 (enterprise sales-assist does not address an SMB price attack or a self-serve funnel regression, and we lack sales capacity to test it in one week), memory_57 (referral incentives amplify an existing base rather than repair a leaking funnel, and would compound rather than diagnose the decline), or memory_91 (activation messaging is a plausible second choice but sits downstream of onboarding; if onboarding completion is falling, messaging optimises a stage fewer accounts reach). All six inherited memories are lossy summaries whose original effect sizes, durations and populations are unknown to me, and none were measured under a competitor price shock, so I treat their magnitudes as unverified priors rather than facts. Accordingly I want this run as a standard experiment with holdout and pre-registered guardrails on downstream account quality — paid conversion, week-four retention and qualified-revenue-per-signup, not completion rate alone — so that a hollow win is visible before it becomes a broad rollout. If verification shows memory_86's lift never propagated past completion, I will switch the slot to activation_messaging.
